World Bank project: Second Community Action for Landscape Management Program for Results (Ethiopia, approved 2026-04-30, Active, commitment US$200.0M)
This hybrid operation—combining Program-for-Results (PforR) and Investment Project Financing (IPF)—supports the National Strategic Investment Framework for Sustainable Landscape Management (ESIF 2, 2024–2038) by advancing long-term landscape restoration. It aims to: (i) expand sustainable land management in degraded Highland Areas; (ii) sustain and expand certification, registration, and digitalization of rural land rights in Ethiopia’s highlands, including communal forests and grazing lands; and (iii) raise farm incomes and create jobs by strengthening agribusiness value-chain linkages. Primary beneficiaries are smallholder farmers in program watersheds. The program will increase smallholders’ livelihood security and broaden income earning opportunities. Efforts will be made for the equitable inclusion of all beneficiaries in Community Watershed Users’ Cooperative Societies (CWUCS) including vulnerable groups such as landless, youth, elderly, and female-headed households.The PforR component will finance watershed-level sustainable land and natural resource management, strengthen rural land administration, improve tenure security for private and communal lands (including selected forests and grazing areas), and catalyze private-sector participation to ensure sustainability.

metadata.title: Second Community Action for Landscape Management Program for Results

content: Under Result Area 1 (Participatory Watershed and Forest Management), Disbursement-Linked Indicators (DLIs) incentivize scaling up restoration and market linkages by: (1) registering Community Watershed Users’ Cooperative Societies (CWUCS) with participatory, approved Watershed Management Plans; (2) expanding the area under sustainable landscape management; (3) establishing Participatory Forest Management with legally recognized cooperatives and approved Forest Management Plans; (4) treating acid soils; (5) integrating cooperatives into existing and new value chains within program catchments; and (6) verifying non forest emission reductions. Under Result Area 2 (Rural Land Administration), DLIs focus on expanding and digitizing secure tenure by: (1) issuing Second Level Land Holding Certificates (SLLCs) for individual parcels; (2) issuing SLLCs for communal forests and grazing lands; (3) operationalizing the National Rural Land Administration Information System in program woredas with digitized SLLCs; and (4) increasing connectivity of land administration offices and systems to national digital infrastructure. The IPF component—financed by IDA, SCALE, Nordic Development Fund (NDF), and ENABLE—will provide cross-cutting technical assistance and capacity building across both result areas and the broader government program (ESIF 2). It will support: (i) agribusiness development by linking landholders to agribusinesses; (ii) design and implementation of payment for ecosystem services (PES) schemes; (iii) access to carbon markets; and (iv) Operationalize pilots to promote voluntary land consolidation in Ethiopia’s highlands. These pilots involve baseline surveys, voluntary land exchange, and design, testing, and documentation of a computerized platform in real-world conditions. The likelihood and magnitude of risk for the voluntary exchange program pilot have been assessed.

metadata.title: Second Community Action for Landscape Management Program for Results

content: The voluntary land exchange will take place in 12 designated kebeles, involving small parcels of land and following a national legal proclamation.Targeted TA will also promote inclusive alternative livelihoods for women and youth through group-based training and livelihood grants; strengthen community capacity to scale ecosystem conservation and carbon sequestration via participatory forest and watershed management; advance land tenure and property rights awareness; and establish community-based performance monitoring. In addition, the operation will enhance MoA and Ethiopia Forest Development (EFD) operational capacity for CALM 2, including: (i) environmental and social risk management; (ii) procurement and financial management; and (iii) monitoring, reporting, and verification, including advanced remote sensing. IFC will complement implementation with integrated upstream and downstream support for agribusiness linkages, value-chain development, and access to finance, strengthening market access and supply chains through its portfolio, pipeline, and early-stage leads. IFC’s approach will promote business models that directly engage smallholder farmers and local communities, with close IFC– World Bank collaboration to ensure coordinated delivery.

World Bank project: Montenegro Forest for Shared Prosperity (Montenegro, approved 2026-03-18, Active, commitment US$21.5M)
The proposed project interventions will focus on improving the bioeconomy of Montenegro through the strengthening of economic viability of the forest industry and forest fire management including improvement of the enabling policy and institutional environment. On the one hand it aims at ensuring the sustainability of the supply chain of forest products through sustainable forest management to enhance economic benefits, ecosystem services and carbon sequestration. This includes integrating environmental, economic and social responsible principles and benchmarks into the supply chain management of the forest products. This entails the standardization and certification of forest products to ensure the quality of forest management and production, increasing transparency to curb illegal logging, intensifying forest fire protection, and modernizing forest management system. On the other hand, the proposed project focuses on improving the economic viability of the forest industry in Montenegro to enhance economic benefits and carbon conservation. This includes support to addressing market challenges and developing wood-processing industry. Lastly, the proposed project will also support regulatory developments and institutional capacity building to ensure responsible forest resource management, enhancing informed forest management decisions, improve value-added production, and ensure compliance with international sustainability standards while contributing to the country's economic growth and environmental protection.

metadata.title: Montenegro Forest for Shared Prosperity

content: The proposed project’s design consists of four components: Component 1: Institutional Capacity Development and System Modernization; Component 2: Enhancing Climate Resilience and Information Services; Component 3: Strengthening Productivity and Sustainable Growth of the Forest Industry; and Component 4: Project Management, Monitoring and Communication. Component 1. Institutional Capacity Development and System Modernization. The objective of this component is to improve the enabling conditions for a stronger Montenegro forest industry and improved the supply chain of forest products to spur economic growth and shared prosperity. The component will facilitate the development of a favorable regulatory environment as well as removal of constraints for forest industry growth and management. The component will focus on the following core interventions: improving policy environment, institutional capacity development, system modernization, and supporting government’s reform of the forest governance including the effective implementation of the new Forest Law. Component 2. Enhancing Climate Resilience and Information Services. The objective of this component of the project is to enhance climate resilience of the forest resources through prevention of forest fires, ensuring the sustainable supply of raw materials to the forest industry, improving informed forest management decisions, and improving the measurement of carbon stocks. The component focuses on the quantification of forest resources and carbon stocks, fair and efficient timber allocation, reducing the risk of wildfires, and restoring degraded forest lands. Component 3. Strengthening Productivity and Sustainable Growth of the Forest Industry.

metadata.title: Montenegro Forest for Shared Prosperity

content: The objective of this component will be to increase the economic contributions of the forest industry to the national development of Montenegro through expanding access to finance, correcting inefficient manufacturing practices, boosting product diversifications, increasing processing capacity, production of profitable high-value wood products, and creation of more high-paying jobs. Component 4. Project Management, Monitoring, and Communication. This component will finance the operating costs of the Project Implementation Unit (PIU) to carry out the oversight and management functions of the project. This includes activities such as procurement and contract management, financial management, environmental and social risk management, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), stakeholder engagement and communication as well as documentation of lessons learned from project implementation and stakeholders’ efforts to scale-up good practices.

World Bank project: Turkmenistan Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification System for Methane Emissions in the Oil and Gas Sector (Turkmenistan, approved 2026-09-25, Active)
At COP28 in Dubai, Turkmenistan joined the Global Methane Pledge, making the commitment to reduce methane emissions by at least 30% by 2030, compared to 2020 levels. Turkmenistan’s oil and gas sector suffers significant gas losses and is strongly committed to tackling this waste problem but lacks a measurement-based methane emissions inventory and consistent monitoring and verification standards. The Ministry of Environmental Protection (MEP) is responsible for coordinating the implementation of the Global Methane Pledge, while State Concern "Turkmennebit" (TN) and State Concern "Turkmengas" (TG) are responsible for operating state-owned oil and gas assets in the country. The Project aims to provide the Government of Turkmenistan and its state-owned operators with a monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) framework and the tools to manage and reduce methane emissions from the (predominantly state-owned) oil and gas sector in the country. Step by step, the Project aims to change this context into action as follows.Component A - Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification System for Methane Emissions in the Oil and Gas Sector: Functional design, technical design, and implementation of a basic MRV system housed at MEP, comprising a sector-wide data repository to collect, store, and analyze source‑level measurement-based emissions data submitted by operators, methodologies, reporting templates, QA/QC protocols, and verification procedures.

metadata.title: Turkmenistan Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification System for Methane Emissions in the Oil and Gas Sector

content: The Project is centered around the design and implementation of an MRV system for methane emissions, essentially a database that will serve as the basis for the Government to collect measured methane emission data from oil and gas operators at the "source level", that is, at the level of individual emission sources, to develop a baseline and set targets for methane emission reduction, to develop a mitigation action plan, and to prescribe (mandatory and voluntary) actions to be taken by TN and TG to reduce methane emissions from state-owned assets in accordance with government policy.Component B - Regulatory Framework for Monitoring, Reporting and Verification of Methane Emissions: Develop (secondary) legislation comprising regulations and technical standards for methane emission reporting aligned with international oil and gas industry standards and best practice. This includes the development of an inspection and compliance function at MEP. The Project aims to support the development of a regulatory framework and institutional capacity for MEP to carry out its mandate to reduce methane emissions.Component (C) - Capacity Building and Training, including Equipment: Capacity building at MEP, TN, and TG in managing and interpreting the results from a gas loss detection and assessment program at an oil and gas facility, including the procurement of methane cameras and gas flow measurement equipment and training in the use of such equipment. Project activities are accompanied by investments in training and capacity building to develop a sustainable methane management function in MEP, TN, and TG beyond the horizon of the Project.Component (D) - Gas Loss Detection and Assessment at Selected Oil and Gas Facilities: Gas loss detection and assessment programs carried out at five representative, priority oil and gas assets of TN and five representative, priority oil and gas assets of TG, across upstream, midstream, and downstream operations.

metadata.title: Turkmenistan Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification System for Methane Emissions in the Oil and Gas Sector

content: Selection criteria for priority assets include a) expected material gas losses based on legacy operator data, third-party data, screening data, and operating characteristics, b) anticipated opportunities to develop high-impact projects, and c) operational accessibility, manageable operational risk, and readiness of site teams. Recognizing that collecting emission data is typically the responsibility of the operator, the Project comprises pilot gas loss detection and assessment programs at selected state-owned assets operated by TN and TG, with the objective to populate the system with actual and actionable measurement-based methane emission data at the source level, to train operator and ministerial staffComponent (E) - First State Gas Loss Reduction Action Plan for the Oil and Gas Sector: Development of a measurement-based, source-level methane emissions baseline and a first State Methane Emission Reduction Action Plan for selected oil and gas assets, presenting a) low-cost opportunities that can be implemented by TN and TG using available personnel and spare parts, and within existing budgets, and b) higher-cost, high-impact methane emission abatement opportunities, screened and ranked for possible future investment financing. The Project is expected to result in a first State Gas Loss Reduction Action Plan, addressing some of the most efficient opportunities first, that is, opportunities for TN and TG to reduce gas losses with low and even negative costs per tonne of methane reduced.

The Project will establish a financial Facility under the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MoEF) for gas leak repair in legacy state-owned gas assets, thereby reducing gas losses, and improving capacity of the operator to manage emissions. The Project will support repair works at the state-owned gas transmission system operator (TSO) Uztransgaz (UTG) only. The Facility will kick off with an initial USD 10 million grant from the GFMR trust fund and will be topped up with financial savings resulting from gas leak repair over time, which will be re-invested into the Facility, mobilizing additional capital for further rehabilitation of the country’s legacy gas infrastructure. While repairing gas leaks is expected to yield significant financial savings, and may even be cash-positive, grant funding from GFMR is needed to start up the proposed scheme, given the current, difficult financial position of UTG.The Project comprises three components: (A) “Repair of gas leaks”; (B) “Capacity building of UTG to monitor and report gas losses and emissions reduction"; (C) “Establishment of the Facility and project implementation support”.Component A: Repair of gas leaks. This is the main component of the Project, funding repair of legacy gas infrastructure according to the original design specifications, including replacement of small parts that are beyond repair. Notably, this means that project funds will not be used to construct new gas transmission facilities, nor will they be used to significantly increase the capacity of existing facilities. The work will be confined within the fence of facilities owned and operated by UTG, in line with national HSE legislation and regulations. Notably, this implies that project funds will not be used to carry out work on third-party land.

metadata.title: Uzbekistan Gas Leak Repair Facility

content: As and when gas leaks are detected, gas leak repair activities will be proposed for funding through the Facility by UTG on a regular basis, according to pre-agreed eligibility criteria and prioritized based on the estimated cost vs. the expected emission reduction potential. Component A also includes procurement of gas leak detection and measurement equipment, personal protection equipment for working on-site, and digital solutions for monitoring methane emissions. Periodically, UTG will report gas savings resulting from leak repair to MoEF according to a pre-agreed protocol, and a pre-agreed portion of the associated financial savings will be set aside for re-investment in the Facility during a pre-agreed period of time.Component B: Capacity building of UTG to monitor and report gas losses and emissions reduction. This component comprises activities to develop the organization of UTG to carry out measurement, monitoring, reporting, and verification (MMRV) of methane emissions in line with international standards and best practices in the oil and gas industry, in particular the Oil and Gas Methane Partnership (OGMP) 2.0 Gold standard. Specifically, the Project will provide technical support to UTG to achieve the OGMP 2.0 Gold Standard Pathway status. Component C: Establishment of the Facility and project implementation support. The Project will include a project implementation support component for procurement of consultancy services by the Implementing Agency to carry out project implementation tasks. This also pertains to consultancy services needed by MoEF to carry out its supervisory role.

World Bank project: Azerigas Gas Leak Detection and Repair Facility (Azerbaijan, approved 2026-08-06, Pipeline)
Azerigas is a ring-fenced business unit of the State Oil Company of the republic of Azerbaijan (SOCAR), with unbundled accounts, responsible for distribution and sales of natural gas to the domestic market in Azerbaijan. The company is experiencing significant gas leaks (fugitive methane emissions) from its legacy assets, most of which are more than fifty years old, estimated at 160 million m3/year (107 kilotonnes per annum (ktpa) CH4). Analysis suggests that around eighty percent by volume of these gas leaks can be repaired with straightforward and cost-effective interventions within a 7-year time period. Using a global warming potential (GWP) factor of 28, this would result in greenhouse gas (GHG) abatement of 2.4 million metric tonnes per annum (mmtpa) CO2e. The project will establish a recipient-executed financial Facility for gas leak detection and repair (LDAR) in the gas distribution system operated by Azerigas. The Facility will be launched with an initial grant from the GFMR trust fund. SOCAR will be the Recipient of the grant and the holder of grant and Facility accounts, and Azerigas will be the sole beneficiary of the grant and the implementing entity responsible for day-to-day implementation and project management. The money will be reallocated from SOCAR to Azerigas for agreed leak detection and repair activities to reduce fugitive emissions of methane on a rolling basis. The project will build on learnings from Azerigas’ pilot gas leak baseline program in Baku. Repair activities will be proposed and implemented by Azerigas according to preliminary agreed eligibility criteria.

metadata.title: Azerigas Gas Leak Detection and Repair Facility

content: Proposed activities will be prioritized based on cost, complexity, impact, and other relevant criteria to maximize the amount of emissions reduced per US$ deployed.In order to guarantee a longer term impact, a key aspect of the proposed financial Facility will be that majority of financial benefits resulting from gas savings as a consequence of leak repair will be re-invested into the Facility, so as to mobilize additional capital to further rehabilitate Azerigas assets. Furthermore, the GFMR-funds initially and the Facility subsequently will be used to build capacity within Azerigas to carry out monitoring, reporting and verification (MRV) of emissions in line with the OGMP 2.0 standard.GFMR grant funding will enable activities that would otherwise not take place due to the strained and constrained financial situation of Azerigas, unlocking methane emission abatement action within the current decade.

World Bank project: Green Urban Development Project (China, approved 2025-06-27, Active, commitment US$250.0M)
The project is premised on the dual agenda of low-carbon and nature-positive urban development which are essential, interconnected strategies for building livable cities. Low-carbon cities focus on planning, implementing, monitoring, and accounting for low-carbon investments and climate change mitigation. Nature-positive cities prioritize urban development that enhances resilience and livability by integrating nature. A joint approach applied in strategic areas that integrates multi-sectoral interventions, offers solutions to the intertwined challenges of climate change and nature loss, and creates mutually reinforcing benefits essential for long-term economic transformation and building sustainable, livable cities. The project intervention area focuses on the Aha Lake area, strategically located in the core of Guiyang city. It is designated as a national wetland park in 2015, serves as a critical urban green lung with important flood control and biodiversity functions. It is recognized that a single project cannot achieve all nature-positive goals or resolve all climate-related issues in Guiyang. Instead, the project targets Aha Lake, which embodies key urban development challenges and high potential, to demonstrate an integrated approach to these goals.

metadata.title: Green Urban Development Project

content: These efforts are further supported by city-wide interventions and innovations on low-carbon platforms, nature-positive planning, and enhanced collaboration.The project will include the following three components: Component 1 (Low-carbon Urban Mobility for Enhanced Livability): This component will finance improvements and constructions around the Aha Lake, focusing on: (i) NMT network and connections to city-wide green network; (ii) public transit connections, including road upgrades for last mile bus connections to metro stations, facilities (bus interchanges, integrated visitor and transit facilities) and services (intelligent transport systems, improved bus coverage, frequency and service); (iii) road connections to and between key city thoroughfares; (iv) integrated visitor/parking facilities and amenities including EV charging stations and bicycle stands; and (v) traffic and transport management. Component 2 (Conserve and Enhance Urban Ecosystems and Biodiversity): This component will finance interventions to improve water quality, enhance flood control, and conserve urban ecosystems and biodiversity. It will reduce GHG emissions by decreasing water pollutants and untreated wastewater, thus reducing methane and nitrous oxide , and enhance the lake's carbon sequestration. Activities under subcomponent 2.2 will restore terrestrial and aquatic habitats and conserve biodiversity. In the long term, this component will improve resilience through better flood management and cooling effects, enhance livability, and create jobs and innovation in environmental conservation, water management, and eco-tourism.

metadata.title: Green Urban Development Project

content: Component 3 (City-Wide Institutional Strengthening for Low-Carbon and Nature-Positive Urban Development): This component will finance city-wide initiatives to support the project’s sustainability, including: (i) technical analysis and development of low-carbon and nature positive urban spatial plans; (ii) research and technical assistance for policies, regulations, and plans on carbon sequestration, carbon market mechanisms, low-carbon transport for vulnerable groups, and behavioral change towards low-carbon lifestyles; and (iii) project management, capacity building, coordination, M&E, and knowledge sharing activities. This component aims to position Guiyang as a front-runner in integrating low-carbon and nature-positive thinking into urban systems, policies and communities.

World Bank project: Additional Financing for Regional Sahel Pastoralism Support Project II Burkina Faso (Western and Central Africa, approved 2024-05-31, Active, commitment US$50.0M)
The proposal is to implement a two-pronged approach to addressing the current food crisis in Burkina Faso. One plank of the proposed support will focus on short term interventions targeting the most vulnerable population. These interventions include: (i) replenishment of the national food security reserve, from which part of the stock will be distributed to vulnerable populations; (ii) animal feed distribution to vulnerable livestock owners; and (iii) procurement and distribution of nutritional supplements to prevent and manage malnutrition. The second pillar of support will focus on the more medium-term interventions to strengthen the resilience and productive capacities of smallholder’s producers to increase production of own food crops and livestock, including: (i) expanding access to quality production inputs (e.g., improved drought resistant seeds, fertilizers/compost); and (ii) improving access to small post-harvest management equipment. Changes to the parent project (the Burkina Faso element) as described below are proposed:Changes to project activities and costs: A total of US$12.1 million in AF resources is allocated to Component 2 (Sustainable landscape management and governance enhancement). Of this, US$1.4 million is allocated to subcomponent 2.1 (Access to natural resources and SLM) to finance a new activity - the construction of 2 biodigesters close to the slaughterhouses in Bobo Dioulasso and Kaya to produce compost/manure for use as a soil fertility amendment in crop production. The manure would be distributed to farmers by the regional directorates in charge of Agriculture in each targeted region based on eligibility criteria to be detailed in the Project Implementation Manual (PIM).

metadata.title: Additional Financing for Regional Sahel Pastoralism Support Project II Burkina Faso

content: Besides helping improve soil fertility for increased production, the biodigesters, each with estimated capacity to produce at least 500 tons of compost per year would also help mitigate methane emissions that would have otherwise escaped from the pits where slaughterhouse waste is currently left to decompose. Under subcomponent 2.2 (Sustainable management of infrastructure for access to water), the parent project finances the construction of pastoral water points in rangelands with no or limited access to water, to ensure the sustainable access of pastoralists to new grazing areas and natural forage resources, and to improve capacity to adapt to climate change. Even with current support, significant gaps in availability of water for both agricultural (crop and livestock production) and household use would persist. The proposal is to allocate US$1.7 million in AF resources to scale up parent project support towards water infrastructure. Specifically, the AF will finance the rehabilitation of 60 climate resilient water points (16 simplified water supply systems, 35 manual boreholes and 9 watering pounds) and the construction of nine (09) boreholes for fodder crops irrigation to protect against climate-induced water scarcity. As in the parent project, the management of this infrastructure would be under the control of beneficiary communities.Another US$9.0 million in AF resources will be committed to subcomponent 2.3 (Fodder production) to scale up parent project support to increasing the availability and accessibility of cultivated fodder to complement the supply of grass - helping to secure pastoral farming and herd mobility and improving resilience.

metadata.title: Additional Financing for Regional Sahel Pastoralism Support Project II Burkina Faso

content: The AF will support the procurement and distribution of 2,100 tons of fertilizers, 750 tons of compost, 1,800 tons of drought resistant dual purpose crop germplasm (e.g., cowpea, sorghum, orange fleshed sweet potato, and maize, among others), as well as 900 tons of fodder crop seeds adapted to the agro-ecological conditions to help producers vulnerable from climate change to increase their food and fodder production. In complement, as new activities, the AF will support the production of compost by producers using locally available materials - where possible, and training on climate-smart production techniques and technologies in the framework of integrated soil fertility management. Additionally, US$9.9 million in AF resources will go towards subcomponent 3.3 (Value-chain development and subproject financing), to scale up parent project financing for improving livestock producer access to critical inputs and small productive assets. Unlike the parent project which under this subcomponent mainly targets producer organizations and the private sector, the A F will target vulnerable small-scale livestock producers, including those that are not part of producer organizations. The AF will support the acquisition and distribution of 13,650 tons of animal feeds, including 9,000 tons of agro-industrial by-products, 1,200 tons of fish feed, 1,950 tons of poultry feed, and 1,500 tons of licking stones. These inputs will be distributed at subsidized rates in compliance with existing government guidelines on inputs subsidies. The distribution will be done by the regional directorates in charge of agriculture and livestock production like the other ongoing projects in the agriculture sector. The AF will also support the improved postharvest management of project supported produce through provision of simple postharvest equipment (e.g., storage containers, cleaners, hand mills, shellers, seed removers, and root crop cutters/graters).

metadata.title: Additional Financing for Regional Sahel Pastoralism Support Project II Burkina Faso

content: Support under this activity will prioritize women, youth, and IDPs. This will diversify livelihoods vulnerable to climate change impacts. Of this, US$3.0 million would go towards supporting the coordination of the AF activities (subcomponent 5.1 – Project coordination) – including enhancing the technical and organizational capacity of the PIU, ensuring environmental and social safeguards compliance, effective M&E, procurement, FM, and communication, among others. SONAGESS has demonstrated capacity to undertake the proposed food procurement and distribution as evidenced under other World Bank - financed projects . The use of IDA resources to purchase food in the current context is a productive investment as it would prevent the continued adoption of negative coping mechanisms by beneficiaries, including the desperate sale of assets. World Bank project: Improving Regional Connectivity and EU Integration (Bosnia and Herzegovina, approved 2027-03-22, Pipeline, commitment US$102.4M)
The Project will support activities that will improve BiH connectivity with EU and ensure sustainable highway financing. Completing the missing link of EU TEN-T Corridor Vc will improve regional, national and international connectivity in the Western Balkans and would ensure the link to EU is fully completed. The project facilitates economic development in the region and will create significant short-term local employment opportunities during highway construction. In addition, the project will improve overall performance of the transport sector by removing some of the through traffic from the local road network reducing congestion, improving safety and resilience of the network connectivity, and rethinking the overall financing scheme for the highway sector in a manner to ensure long term sustainability of the network management. This will be achieved through 2 components: (i) Improved EU integration and regional connectivity and (ii) improved highway network management and financial sustainability in BIH.(i) Improved EU integration and regional connectivity: This component will finance completion of a missing 36.5km link on the EU TEN-T Vc Corridor from Johovac to Vukosavlje. Corridor Vc is the main north-south transport route in BiH and connects Budapest (Hungary) to the Adriatic port of Ploče (Croatia). Within BiH, Corridor Vc’s total length is approximately 335 km. The project section passes through rural areas with a number of linear villages on two existing regional roads: The M-17 (single lane in each direction) passing along the left bank of the River Bosna and the R-465 (single lane in each direction) along the right bank, parallel to the railway road Doboj – Modriča. The alignment passes mainly through a wide plain of predominantly cultivated land.

metadata.title: Improving Regional Connectivity and EU Integration

content: Close to the end of the section the alignment enters the alluvial plain of the Bosna River and remains in the plain until the end. The alluvial plane is often flooded by the Bosna River. The most important structures proposed along the alignment are the cut-and-cover tunnel Dobor (approx. 1 km) and four bridges over the Bosna River (up to 600 m each), and two Trumpet type interchanges. The entire alignment is proposed on the embankment with an average height of 4.25 m. The road will have a design speed of 120 km/h and be approximately 28 m wide and accommodate 2 running lanes of 3.75 m and a hard shoulder of 2x1.5 m and a central reserve of 4 m.Detailed design is available but is more than 5 years old and would need an update. Proposed approach is to use Design and Build contract, where structures and alignment will not be changed but contractor will have opportunity to propose specific construction methodologies and some changes in materials or specifications, as well as the detailing of minor elements such as noise barriers and fencing. Estimated value of the project with contingencies is EUR 500 million. (ii) Improved highway network management and financial sustainability in BIH. In addition to completion of missing TEN-T link, the project will support introduction of ITS along the highway network, selected measures to improve highway network resilience to the natural hazards, and enhancing financial sustainability of the transport sector in general and RS Highway Company in particular. Proposed financing approach: The Project will support the financing by partnering with other IFIs and securing EU grants. Utilizing IBRD and MIGA Guarantee mechanisms will be explored as unique feature of the operation, ensuring the higher participation of the private and commercial sector in the transport management.

World Bank project: Delhi Clean Air Program - Phase 1 (India, approved 2026-11-25, Pipeline, commitment US$130.0M)
The proposed operation is part of the World Bank-financed Regional Air Quality Management (AQM) Program in the Indo-Gangetic Plain and Himalayan Foothills (IGP-HF) region, which supports Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Nepal, and Pakistan in institutional strengthening, emissions reduction, and regional knowledge exchange, forming the foundation of airshed management across the region. In India, the IGP covers around 18 percent of the country's land area and nearly 40 percent of its population, where rapid urbanization and economic growth have driven substantial emissions from transport, industry, road dust, and construction activities, making it a global air pollution hotspot. The Program aligns with India's Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, the National Clean Air Programme (NCAP), India's Nationally Determined Contribution commitments, and interstate airshed directives from the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM).The CAQM estimated the source contributions through a meta-analysis of emissions inventory studies from 2015 to 2025 that were available for Delhi or data shared by a panel of experts convened by CAQM in Identification of the causes for worsening AQI in Delhi National Capital Region (NCR), Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas, January 2026 (CAQM, 2026). Delhi has implemented one of India’s most comprehensive air pollution control programs, combining policy reforms, enforcement measures, infrastructure investments, and sectoral interventions. The government’s commitment is reflected in the Delhi Air Pollution Mitigation Action Plan 2026 and the allocation of a Green Budget of US$2.4 billion (21.44% of total Government of National Capital of Delhi (GNCTD) budget for FY 2026-27) for mainstreaming environmental considerations in government planning and expenditure.

metadata.title: Delhi Clean Air Program - Phase 1

content: However, the complexity of managing emissions across sectors and jurisdictions—particularly given the transboundary nature of sources and evolving meteorological influences—requires strengthened coordination, implementation consistency, and evidence-based decision-making. DCAP Phase 1 is part of a proposed seven-year Multi-Phase Programmatic Approach (MPA), supporting the GNCTD with successive financing operations to manage the complexity of cross-sector interventions and build sustained air quality management systems. The phased approach enables sequencing—from immediate emission reduction actions to longer-term investments and structural reforms—while incorporating learning and scaling across phases. Phase 1 of the Program would focus on: (i) short- to medium-term actions to reduce air pollution from transport sector which is a major source of PM2.5 emissions in Delhi NCT; and (ii) development of a long-term AQM plan and its corresponding institutional framework. Subsequent phases are expected to scale and deepen these interventions and expand support to additional sectors and strengthen policy frameworks based on emerging evidence and priorities for sustained air quality improvements. DCAP Phase 1 would finance a Program for Results (PforR) combined with technical assistance to support GNCTD’s multi-sector effort across two results areas (RAs): 1) Strengthening AQM Planning, Coordination and Citizen Engagement: Global experience demonstrates that a robust AQM framework is crucial to achieving sustained, measurable clean air improvements. Delhi has established an extensive policy and regulatory foundation, as well as a dense air quality monitoring network, which provide a strong platform for further consolidation.

metadata.title: Delhi Clean Air Program - Phase 1

content: Opportunities remain to strengthen multi-sector planning, improve data quality and integration, develop more effective policies and financing instruments, update emissions inventories, and enhance monitoring, enforcement, and inter-agency coordination for enhanced implementation and enforcement of clean air initiatives. A well-designed and sustained communications and behaviour change strategy can also strengthen public awareness, encourage behavioural shifts, and foster broader stakeholder engagement. The first phase would support the GNCTD: (i) develop, adopt and implement a medium-term Air Pollution Management Plan 2027-2031, with defined outcomes, sector targets, budget, institutional and governance arrangements, and M&E systems; (ii) adopt and implement a Clean Air Communications and Behavior Change Strategy (Clean Air CBCS) to increase awareness and promote behavior change for air pollution mitigation and health-protective measures 2) Reducing emissions from transport, through enforcement, electric vehicle transition and enhanced public transport system: Transport plays a significant and complex role in Delhi NCR's air quality crisis, acting as a major year-round contributor to pollution. Transport emissions account for an estimated 19–23% of primary PM2.5 concentrations and 81% of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions in Delhi (CAQM 2026) which is a precursor of secondary particulate matter contributing to PM2.5. Rapid and sustained growth in the vehicle fleet, coupled with significant daily traffic inflows from neighbouring NCR cities—including a high share of heavy-duty diesel vehicles (trucks and buses) that contribute disproportionately to particulate matter emissions—has intensified the problem. This is further exacerbated by the prevalence of older and poorly maintained vehicles with weak emission controls, resulting in real-world emissions that often exceed certified standards.

metadata.title: Delhi Clean Air Program - Phase 1

content: Systematic solutions to decouple growth in transport demand from emissions, while transitioning towards cleaner vehicles, could significantly reduce transport emissions. While electrification presents a major opportunity for emission reduction, the pace of transition is constrained by gaps in charging infrastructure, including inadequate charger density, uneven spatial distribution of charging stations, limited charging options for commercial and heavy-duty vehicles, and challenges related to land availability and grid connectivity. The first phase interventions for transport sector would focus on strengthening enforcement systems and enabling conditions for scaled transition to cleaner and public transport. Key activities would include (i) enhancing enforcement mechanisms to limit entry and operation of high emitting (pre-BS VI vehicles) and end-of-life vehicles; (ii) accelerating EV uptake under the upcoming Delhi EV Policy 2.0, particularly in two- and three-wheelers and goods vehicles, and scaling up public charging infrastructure; (iii) strengthening the electric bus (e-bus) ecosystem through bus service optimization and depot infrastructure readiness; (iv) operationalizing the Delhi Unified Metropolitan Transport Authority (DUMTA) and preparing a Comprehensive Mobility Plan (CMP) for integrated planning and delivery of mobility services in the city. Strategic Alignment to CPF. DCAP is closely aligned with the India CPF FY2026-2031 and with the vision for a Viksit Bharat 2047. The operation would address a critical challenge identified in the CPF - poor air quality - and support the CPF’s emphasis on improved livability, sustainability, and management in the megacity of Delhi NCT.

The proposed operation is the first phase of the Saint Paul 2 Hydropower Project (SP2) Multiphase Programmatic Approach in Liberia. World Bank project: Integrated Resilient Development Project (Viet Nam, approved 2025-09-30, Active, commitment US$145.0M)
The IRDP will finance a targeted package of climate-resilient infrastructure investments in Da Nang City and Gia Lai Province, selected to reduce disaster and climate-related risks, strengthen access to critical services, and support inclusive economic growth. The project adopts a multi-sectoral approach that integrates disaster risk management and climate adaptation considerations into infrastructure development. It is fully aligned with the city’s and province’s Socio-Economic Development Plan (SEDP), masterplans, and investment priorities. The core activities include the construction and rehabilitation of flood drainage systems, multi-purpose flood and storm surge protection works, climate-resilient roads and bridges, and integrated evacuation routes in urban and peri-urban areas. These investments were identified based on detailed flood risk assessments, site-specific hydrological and geotechnical studies, and scenario-based investment prioritization processes. Engineering designs incorporate flood modeling, sea level rise projections, and material specifications to ensure infrastructure durability under both current and future hazard conditions. By targeting critical corridors and vulnerable population clusters, the infrastructure improvements are expected to reduce acute disaster impacts, minimize service disruptions, and protect lives and livelihoods. Co-benefits such as enhanced mobility, safer evacuation access, and reduced economic losses from flooding are embedded in the design.

metadata.title: Integrated Resilient Development Project

content: Climate mitigation is also integrated through the inclusion of energy-efficient street lighting, urban greening, and vegetated embankments, which contribute to carbon sequestration, erosion control, and microclimate regulation.The IRDP will enhance the institutional capacity of Da Nang City and Gia Lai Province to plan, implement, and manage climate-resilient infrastructure systems. Rather than a standalone training component, capacity building is embedded throughout implementation, using a "learning-by-doing" model that provides continuous technical support to local agencies and project teams. This includes structured consultations during the design and procurement phases, hands-on support for engineering reviews and safeguards implementation, and technical assistance in the formulation of risk-informed O&M strategies. Local authorities and provincial departments—such as the DOC and DAE—will benefit from applied learning on climate-resilient design principles, maintenance planning, and interdepartmental coordination mechanisms. The project also promotes knowledge exchange on NbS for flood and erosion protection, including vetiver grass embankments, eco-dredging techniques, and green buffer zones. These approaches are expected to not only increase infrastructure longevity and environmental co-benefits but also serve as demonstration models for replication by other provinces. By facilitating local ownership and institutional learning, the project contributes to the long-term sustainability of climate adaptation investments.To ensure the functionality and resilience of the financed infrastructure over time, the IRDP will support the development of asset-specific, climate-informed O&M plans tailored to the localized flood and storm risk profiles and performance needs of each investment. These plans will serve as practical tools for city and provincial agencies to guide infrastructure upkeep, budgeting, and risk monitoring.

metadata.title: Integrated Resilient Development Project

content: In addition to technical specifications for regular maintenance, they will include protocols for adaptive measures such as sediment control, slope stabilization, and flood flow regulation. Drainage and transport designs also incorporate scalability and modular features to allow for upgrades as climate conditions evolve. The project will institutionalize the use of such tools by embedding them in provincial infrastructure planning cycles and aligning them with national standards. Lessons and models from the IRDP will be documented and disseminated through inter-provincial and inter-agency platforms, supporting the wider adoption of resilient infrastructure practices and informing future iterations of national design guidelines and technical norms.The IRDP will be implemented over a six-year period and organized around two components: Component 1 – Support to Da Nang City, and Component 2 – Support to Gia Lai Province. Each component will finance climate-resilient infrastructure investments and provide support for project management and technical assistance. In Da Nang City, investments will focus on enhancing flood conveyance capacity within the Truong Giang River basin through dredging, hybrid (green and grey) embankment construction, a new flood bypass system with a ship lock and water gate, and the construction of resilient bridges to maintain east-west connectivity. In Gia Lai Province, the project will support the construction of elevated coastal and inland roads and bridges to improve access to Quy Nhon Port and surrounding flood-prone corridors. These investments are based on climate and disaster risk assessments, incorporating climate-resilient design specifications such as elevated roadbeds, slope stabilization, and erosion-resistant materials. Each province will receive implementation support, including detailed engineering design, construction supervision, environmental and social safeguards management, procurement, and project management assistance.

World Bank project: Kenya Contingent Emergency Response Project (Kenya, approved 2026-10-09, Active)
The proposed Kenya Contingent Emergency Response Project (CERP) is a dedicated, pre-positioned financial and delivery instrument designed to enable the Government of Kenya (GoK) to respond promptly and effectively to eligible crises or emergencies, including natural and man-made disasters. The Project Development Objective is to respond promptly and effectively to an eligible crisis or emergency in the Republic of Kenya.Kenya is among Eastern Africa's most disaster-exposed countries, with over 70 percent of natural hazard-induced disasters attributable to extreme climatic events — primarily droughts and floods — at an estimated annual economic cost of 2 to 2.8 percent of GDP. Climate change is intensifying these risks, compounding vulnerabilities for an estimated 3 to 4 million people affected by natural disasters each year. The country is susceptible to non-climatic risks including disease outbreaks.The proposed operation represents a step-change in Kenya's crisis financing architecture, moving from ad hoc Contingent Emergency Response Components (CERCs) embedded within sector projects to a systematic, cross-sectoral emergency financing instrument. Upon activation following a formal GoK request, the CERP would finance emergency response activities across multiple sectors — including emergency livelihood support to households and provision of essential services and supplies — as defined in the CERP Manual and Crisis Response Plan for each activation.The project will be overseen by a Project Steering Committee (PSC), with the Ministry of Agriculture Food Systems Resilience Project (FSRP) PIU serving as the CERP PIU. Implementation will leverage existing World Bank-financed project structures and coordination mechanisms across relevant national ministries and county governments.

content: The operation is aligned with the World Bank Group Country Partnership Framework for Kenya (FY2023–FY2028), in particular CPF Objective 6 on strengthening national systems for disaster preparedness and climate resilience. It also contributes to Kenya's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), National Adaptation Plan (NAP) 2015–2030, and the goals of the Paris Agreement on climate adaptation. The overall project risk rating is Substantial.

World Bank project: Bolivia Resilient Water Management for Community and Household Irrigation Project (Bolivia, approved 2024-02-20, Active, commitment US$150.0M)
The Project will support the implementation of the first phase of the Government of Bolivia's Climate Smart and Resilient Program (Programa Lucho por una Bolivia Climaticamente Inteligente y Resiliente, Fase 1), which is a comprehensive rural development program, covering actions from water conservation, irrigation and risk management investments to information, knowledge management and water governance. It will have a strong focus on adaptation strategies for tackling the impacts of climate change on water security as well as developing resilience to climate change exacerbated flood and drought risks for Bolivia’s poorest communities. The Project will adopt an integrated approach, from basin to micro-basin planning, and will include investments for water management at the micro-basin level, investments for hydrological risk management, as well as investments to secure adequate water for irrigation of rain-fed crops, increasing farmers’ ability to improve food security and reducing their vulnerability to the increasing, climate change-induced rainfall variability. The Project design will consider some basic principles:• A comprehensive analysis of needs at the basin level. Activities or subprojects to secure the availability and sustainable use of water resources for target areas will be identified through a comprehensive analysis of the needs of 15 targeted basins with areas up to 20,000 km2 and the development of basin-level strategic integrated water plans (EPHIC) - formerly known as Basin Master Plans. • Micro-basins as the basic geographic unit. Project interventions will target micro-basins spanning less than around 200 km2 (operational hydrographic units), whose management units are OGCs. These micro-basins form part of larger basins managed by UGCs.

metadata.title: Bolivia Resilient Water Management for Community and Household Irrigation Project

content: Most of the micro-basins are located within the territory of one or a few autonomous municipal governments, thus facilitating coordination with the OGCs. In turn, larger basins that are managed by UGCs oftentimes extend beyond the boundaries of a single department and require the involvement of and closer coordination with the autonomous departmental governments and the MMAyA/VRHR. For activities under the VRHR’s responsibilities and that are eligible for Project funding, pre-feasibility studies (Technical Reports on Preconditions, ITCPs) and detailed technical designs (Pre-investment Technical Design Studies, EDTPs) will be prepared. In the case of activities that are not under the VRHR’s responsibilities or are not eligible for financing under the Project, subproject profiles will be prepared to help stakeholders - municipal governments and community organizations such as OGCs - look for other funding sources.• A bottom-up approach. The activities or subprojects will be identified and prioritized by the communities with the active participation of the municipal governments and the OGCs. The Project’s target will be basins located in the 9 departments of Bolivia. The geographic area comprises 256 municipal governments. Eligibility criteria for the selection of these basins include: (i) high aridity index, (ii) high levels of poverty, (iii) high population density, and (iv) potential areas of intervention under the different components of the Project. The Project will sequence the activities to focus initially on basins that present high levels of need and high levels of readiness for implementation, tackling ‘low-hanging fruits’ quickly to demonstrate early successes in the first phase of the Bolivia Climate Smart and Resilient Program and inform the design of the following phases. The Project will comprise of the following four components:Component 1. Water resources planning and pre-investment studies (US$9.930 million).

metadata.title: Bolivia Resilient Water Management for Community and Household Irrigation Project

content: This component will fund studies with two objectives: (i) development of water management plans at the basin level that follow both IWRM and integrated water basin management (MIC) approaches. This task will involve the identification and analysis of the main challenges the basins face from a territorial and sectoral perspective, and the development of a strategic vision based on the sustainable use of water resources; and (ii) development of pre-investment studies and detailed engineering designs for the subprojects, related to water conservation, irrigation, and risk management infrastructure, identified in each basin water management plan. Component 2. Climate resilient infrastructure investments (US$139.619 million). This component will fund works and the supervision of investments related to water conservation, soil and land management, irrigation, and risk management to adapt to the impacts of and to build resilience against climate change exacerbated floods and droughts. The component will be divided into three sub-components.• Subcomponent 2.1. Investments in integrated water basins management (MIC). Investments will include activities to protect water sources, water planting and harvesting, soil improvement, protection of water recharge areas and recovery of forest areas. These investments aim to reduce the vulnerability of watersheds facing degradation and desertification, and to increase water availability and local storage capacity. The investments will also enhance soil and crop carbon stock. • Subcomponent 2.2: Community and household irrigation systems.

metadata.title: Bolivia Resilient Water Management for Community and Household Irrigation Project

content: The investments in household and community irrigation systems, which are classified as minor irrigation systems by the VRHR, will include infrastructure for water capture (harvesting of surface runoff, groundwater extraction, use of spring water and other alternative water sources), the installation of water storage solutions, the conveyance of water to the field, and the equipment necessary for water distribution on the plots. • Subcomponent 2.3: Risk management infrastructure. This subcomponent will support infrastructure to protect land and communities against extreme hydrological events, including flooding, and to conserve, restore and manage soils degraded by erosion. Component 3: Capacity building for water governance and enhanced productivity (US$16.622 million). This component will fund technical assistance (TA) and capacity building activities to enhance water governance at the national, macro, regional and basins level. The component will include TA and training for UGCs, OGCs, municipal governments, and farmers.Component 4. Project management (US$5.317 million). This component will fund activities to support Project administration and management, including procurement, financial, environmental, social, and technical management as well as audits and monitoring and evaluation (M&E).

World Bank project: Morupule B Generation and Transmission Project (Botswana, approved 2009-10-29, Closed)
The objectives of the Morupule B Generation and Transmission Project are to support Botswana in: (i) developing reliable and affordable supply of electricity for energy security; (ii) promoting alternative energy resources for low-carbon growth; and (iii) building its institutional capacity in the energy sector. There are three components to the project. The first component of the project is Morupule generation expansion. This component, to be implemented by Botswana Power Corporation (BPC), includes three distinct and integral infrastructure subcomponents as follows: the first sub-component is Morupule B power station involves construction of a 600 MW coal-fired power station, adjacent to the existing Morupule A Power Station near Palapye, in the eastern part of the country; the second sub-component is transmission system involves construction, supply and installation of: (a) Morupule Phokoje 400 kV transmission line (102 kilometer (km) and associated equipment; and (b) Morupule-Isang 400 kV transmission line (215 km) and associated equipment; and the third sub-component of the project is water supply system involves construction of: (a) pipeline from the new Paje well field to the Morupule B Power Station (80 km) for backup supply; and (b) power supply line for the new Paje well field. The second component of the project is alternative energy development. This component will support diversification of Botswana's economy through a low-carbon growth strategy. Given Botswana's energy endowment, its cleaner fuel options are to develop coal-bed methane and to explore solar thermal, while examining prospects for carbon capture and storage as a means to mitigate climate change impacts. The third component of the project is institution and capacity building.

World Bank project: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Clean Air Project (Pakistan, approved 2027-03-25, Pipeline, commitment US$200.0M)
The Project is aligned with World Bank Group corporate and regional priorities. The Pakistan Country Partnership Framework (CPF) 2026–35 includes an Outcome Area “Cleaner energy and better air quality” with a target of “35% reduction of the population-weighted PM2.5 average annual exposure from 55 to 35μg/m3”, consistent with goals set out in Pakistan’s National Clean Air Policy and the World Health Organization’s first interim target. A “35 by 35” goal to achieve 35ug/m3 by 2035 was also adopted collectively among the Indo-Gangetic Plain and Himalayan Foothills Region countries in 2024. The project will additionally contribute to CPF Outcome Areas on “Reduced child stunting”, and “Increased resilience to climate change”. The project activities focus on strengthening Provincial AQM systems through a convergence of work across government departments led by the Chief Minister and Chief Secretary Offices, the KP Climate Change, Forestry, Environment and Wildlife Department, and the Planning and Development Department in cooperation with other sector departments. The project will enhance air quality monitoring, governance, and enforcement, and implement selected cost-effective emission reduction measures from major contributing sectors. Investments in transport, household cooking, and waste will focus on Peshawar and surrounding districts to demonstrate good practice models for future scale-up; while industry investments involving policy reforms and regulatory practices will be implemented Province-wide. The following project components are proposed:Component 1: Air Quality Management and Governance.

metadata.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Clean Air Project

content: This component will help build KP Province’s capacity for convergence of inter-departmental action and evidence-based decision making to improve air quality in line with the KP Smog Action Plan while strengthening regulatory, institutional, and technical capabilities. Project-funded activities will improve air quality and climate change data collection to support assessment and monitoring by establishing a network of regulatory-grade monitoring stations, creating a central decision support system, and developing an integrated pollutant and greenhouse gas emissions inventory. It also includes a comprehensive source apportionment study, a multi-year public awareness campaign focused on air pollution and its health impacts, and the introduction of an interdepartmental coordination and monitoring systems for air quality and climate change activities and results. Component 2: Sector Transition Programs. This component will support implementation of first stage clean air measures for emission reductions in sectors selected from - transport, household energy, industry, and solid waste management as the largest contributors to PM₂.₅ exposure in the Peshawar Valley. The KP Smog Action Plan, World Bank analytics, and stakeholder discussions identified priority near-term high-impact, cost-effective measures that are most critical to reduce exposure within Peshawar District taking into consideration broader airshed dynamics. Activities under this component will combine policy reforms and institutional strengthening with physical investments to demonstrate scalable models for province-wide adoption. Work on component 1 will be carried out alongside efforts to implement the Sector-based Clean Air Transition programs, helping to develop and revise plans for new measures in later phases.Component 3: Contingent Emergency Response. This component will provide immediate response to an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, as needed.

World Bank project: First Advancing Global Integration and Market Transition Uzbekistan Programmatic Development Policy Operation (Uzbekistan, approved 2025-10-10, Active, commitment US$800.0M)
The development objective of the First Advancing Global Integration and Market Transition Development Policy Operation for Uzbekistan is to support Uzbekistan’s transition to an inclusive and resilient market economy through: (i) creating markets, advancing global integration, and fostering private sector growth and jobs creation; and (ii) supporting the green economy and social inclusion. Under the first pillar it will focus on promoting more competitive markets in telecom, electricity, heating and agricultural sectors, as well as reducing the presence of the state in competitive markets (a combination of privatization and advancing competitive neutrality, notably towards state-owned enterprises (SOEs)). This first pillar also supports reforms to deepen Uzbekistan’s integration into global trade, including those required to secure World Trade Organization (WTO) membership. The second pillar supports reforms to lower greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions through renewable energy, energy efficiency and reforms in agriculture, and reforms to promote climate resilience, especially in the agricultural sector, by directly addressing the identified sectoral climate risks. The second pillar also supports reforms to create a more inclusive economy by strengthening social protection and social insurance and addressing gender discrimination.

World Bank project: Sustainable Urban and Peri-Urban Agriculture for Women Empowerment Project (Liberia, approved 2026-09-11, Active)
The project aims to enhance the productivity, resilience, and market access for women and youth vegetable farmers in urban and peri-urban Liberia. This is crucial because Liberia's agri-food sector, despite being a major economic pillar, suffers from low horticultural productivity and heavy reliance on food imports, leading to food system inefficiency and poor nutrition. Rapid urbanization is increasing demand for fresh vegetables, but domestic production is hampered by climate stressors like erratic rainfall, rising temperatures, and flooding, which undermine productivity and resilience, especially for smallholder farmers dependent on rainfed systems. Additionally, the sector faces challenges such as low productivity, weak production systems, food safety gaps, fragmented markets, institutional capacity deficits, and significant gender and youth exclusion. The project seeks to address these issues by promoting climate-smart agriculture, improving market linkages, and empowering women and youth in the vegetable value chain.It complements the ongoing World Bank support for community vegetable and kitchen gardening under RETRAP. The proposal is to focus on urban and peri-urban horticulture as this offers the highest potential to simultaneously advance food and nutrition security, jobs, and climate resilience objectives. First, over 52 percent of the Liberian population now lives in urban hubs, creating concentrated demand for fresh food. Second, focusing investments around these areas, rather than in deep rural areas, helps bypass Liberia’s road infrastructure gap, by positioning production proximate to the consumer which effectively reduces post-harvest losses and greenhouse gas emissions associated with produce transportation.

metadata.title: Sustainable Urban and Peri-Urban Agriculture for Women Empowerment Project

content: Third, it offers the best prospects for reducing foreign exchange outflows associated with horticultural imports as most of these are destined for urban consumption. Fourth, because urban retail food markets in Liberia are dominated by "market women", whose profit margins are suppressed by the erratic pricing of imported produce, localizing production gives them direct, stable access to cheaper, fresher inventory, which is key to their economic empowerment. Finally, Liberia’s urban and peri-urban areas are flooded with underemployed youth. Peri-urban horticulture can leverage agile technology, transforming agriculture into attractive job opportunities for the youth.The proposed operation is firmly anchored in Liberia's national development priorities, directly supporting the ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development (AAID) 2025–2029, specifically Pillar 1 on economic transformation, which envisions a competitive, diversified, and resilient private sector-led economy with agriculture at its center. This vision is operationalized through the National Agricultural Development Plan (NADP), which identifies horticulture, and vegetables in particular, as a priority value chain for income growth, food and nutrition security, and productive employment. The support is also consistent with Outcome 4 (Increased private investment, with a focus on agroindustry and forestry) of the World Bank Group's Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for Liberia (FY2025–2030), especially the intention to improve the productivity of select agriculture value chains. To the extent that the project contributes to food and nutrition security, as well as job creation, it is also aligned with the Mission AgriConnect, which aims to create more and better jobs, raise smallholder incomes, and strengthen food security.

metadata.title: Sustainable Urban and Peri-Urban Agriculture for Women Empowerment Project

content: Finally, the project supports the Japan Social Development Fund (JSDF) objectives by empowering vulnerable groups through targeted training and capacity-building for urban and peri-urban vegetable farmers.The activities under the grant application will be organized around 3 components:Component 1: Support for Development of Smart Modern Community Vegetable Gardens.The component will support the establishment market-oriented, modern community vegetable gardens (5–10 hectares each) across 30 communities, equipped with climate-smart irrigation systems (drip or sprinkler) and solar-powered water systems, along with multipurpose sheds and sanitary facilities. This activity will also support the formation and strengthening of gardeners’ associations, including capacity building in organizational management and the installation, operation, and maintenance of irrigation systems. It will provide tailored training for urban and peri-urban women and youth in market-oriented horticulture production, focusing on sustainable and climate-smart practices, modern inputs and technologies, and improved market linkages, including hands-on capacity building for irrigation infrastructure operation and maintenance. The project will also promote nutrition-sensitive interventions for vulnerable groups to increase the availability, access, and utilization of nutrient-dense vegetables, supporting behavior change and awareness initiatives to improve dietary diversity and nutrition outcomes.Component 2: Support for Farmer Coordination, Institutional Strengthening and Market Linkages.The component seeks to improve market access by organizing farmers into groups, strengthening cooperatives, supporting business skills, enhancing food safety and quality standards, and building linkages with supermarkets, hotels, hospitals, and regional markets. It also invests in private sector partnerships, post-harvest infrastructure, certification systems, and digital market tools.

metadata.title: Sustainable Urban and Peri-Urban Agriculture for Women Empowerment Project

content: Component 3 covers project management, monitoring and evaluation—linked to RETRAP—and knowledge dissemination. It ensures effective implementation, learning, and visibility of support from the Government of Japan.The project will be implemented in urban and peri‑urban communities across six counties in Liberia—Montserrado, Bong, Margibi, Grand Bassa, Bomi, and Nimba—where horticulture represents a predominant livelihood activity for rural households.The primary target beneficiaries of the project are women and youth groups, including persons with disabilities, who are engaged or able to participate in urban and peri urban vegetable gardening in Liberia. The project is expected to directly benefit approximately 15,000 urban and peri urban vegetable value chain actors, many of whom currently face constraints related to seasonal production, overreliance on rain fed agriculture, low productivity, and limited access to markets due to poor product quality. It will strengthen the capacity of a broader set of actors within the vegetable value chain, including SMEs, aggregators, traders, and public and non public service providers who support production, aggregation, and market linkages. By addressing these systemic constraints and enhancing the skills and market readiness of beneficiaries, the project is expected to significantly improve food and nutritional security, as well as the income levels of women, youth, and their households.
